questions.question: What does a voltmeter measure?
questions.tutor: Voltmeter measures potential difference between two points.

questions.question: How is a voltmeter connected in a circuit?
questions.tutor: Voltmeter connects in parallel to measure voltage across a component.

questions.question: How is an ammeter connected in a circuit?
questions.tutor: Ammeter connects in series to measure current through a branch.

questions.question: What is the ideal resistance of an ammeter?
questions.tutor: Ideal ammeter has zero resistance to avoid voltage drop.

questions.question: What is the ideal resistance of a voltmeter?
questions.tutor: Ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance to avoid loading the circuit.

questions.question: What does an ohmmeter measure?
questions.tutor: Ohmmeter measures resistance, typically with internal battery.

questions.question: What is a multimeter?
questions.tutor: Multimeter combines voltmeter, ammeter, and ohmmeter functions.

questions.question: What does a wattmeter measure?
questions.tutor: Wattmeter measures real power (watts) in AC or DC circuits.

questions.question: How many coils does an analog wattmeter have?
questions.tutor: Electrodynamometer wattmeter has fixed current coil and moving voltage coil.

questions.question: What does a power factor meter measure?
questions.tutor: Power factor meter measures cosine of angle between voltage and current.

questions.question: What instrument measures energy consumption?
questions.tutor: KWh meter (electric meter) measures energy consumption over time.

questions.question: What does a clamp meter measure?
questions.tutor: Clamp meter measures current via magnetic coupling, no direct contact.

questions.question: What is the principle of a moving coil instrument?
choices: Current in coil interacts with permanent magnet
questions.tutor: PMMC uses current in coil interacting with permanent magnet field.

questions.question: What is the advantage of a digital multimeter (DMM)?
questions.tutor: DMM offers high accuracy, high input impedance, and digital readout.

questions.question: What is an oscilloscope used for?
questions.tutor: Oscilloscope displays voltage vs time waveform.

questions.question: What is the function of a current transformer (CT)?
questions.tutor: CT reduces high primary current to standard 5A or 1A for meters.

questions.question: What is the function of a potential transformer (PT)?
questions.tutor: PT steps down high voltage to standard 110V for meters.

questions.question: What is the secondary rating of a standard CT?
questions.tutor: Standard CT secondary is 5 A (or 1 A for some systems).

questions.question: What is the secondary rating of a standard PT?
questions.tutor: Standard PT secondary is 110 V (line-to-line).

questions.question: What does a thermocouple measure?
questions.tutor: Thermocouple generates voltage proportional to temperature difference.
